label: Postgres: Update Rows
description: Update the rows matching a SQL condition, setting columns from a JSON object, and emit the changed rows. A `vector` or `halfvec` column takes a list of numbers and comes back as one. A table with a column the node cannot read back (`sparsevec`, `point`, ...) is refused before any row changes; update it with Postgres: Query instead. A changed value it cannot read back (a two-dimensional array in an `int4[]` column) undoes the update, so no row changes. The condition's parameters are the node's own inline-declared input ports, read by name, as in Postgres: Query: `PostgresUpdateRows(email: String) { where: "email = $email" }`. Unreachable database or a broken constraint: catchable by `_error`. `count` is every changed row; `rows` holds as many of them as fit the 100 KB a wire carries, and `truncated` says when some were left out. A syntax error in `where`, an unknown column, a column it cannot read back, or a `$name` with no port of that name: always fails the run.

inputs.name: account
inputs.description: Wire a PostgresAccess, or a PostgresDatabase's access output.

inputs.name: where
inputs.label: Where
inputs.description: SQL condition; each `$name` reads the inline-declared input port of that name. `true` updates every row.

outputs.name: rows
outputs.description: Changed rows as stored, as many as fit the 100 KB a wire carries.

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: How many rows the update changed, all of them, whether or not `rows` holds them all.

outputs.name: truncated
outputs.description: True when the changed rows weighed more than a wire carries, so `rows` holds only the first ones. The update itself changed every row either way.
